text.p: A powerful bomb killed at least 10 people in a bustling street in central Algiers on Sunday evening, hours after Moslem rebels slaughtered 36 people overnight in a village in north Algeria.
"I counted at least 10 bodies and I saw more than 50 wounded," said one resident of the blast scene in Belouizdad street in Belcourt district of Algiers.
Another resident, speaking by telephone from Algiers, said the bomb had been hidden in a bag and exploded near a crowded cafe and a cinema known as Cinema Musset.
The bomb, the second in Algiers in 12 days, followed the massacre of villagers in Medea province, a stronghold of the feared Armed Islamic Group (GIA).
The official Algerian news agency APS quoted an Algerian security forces statement as saying 36 people were killed in Sidi Abdelaziz village in Medea province, 70 km (40 miles) south of Algiers.

The killing was the bloodiest in a series of massacres, mostly in remote villages, and bombings in Algiers and surrounding towns in which more than 300 people have died in the past two-and-a-half months.
The security forces blamed the massacre on a "group of terrorists", the term the authorities use to describe Moslem guerrillas in Algeria.
The Sunday evening bomb ripped through Belouizdad street during rush hour as residents ended their daily fast during the Moslem month of Ramadan.
"Limbs of the victims, many of them hawkers in the street, were strewn on the pavement," said one resident.
Emergency services rushed the scene to ferry the wounded to hospitals and security forces sealed the area, residents said.

A powerful bomb killed 14 people and wounded more than 100 in a crowded car market on Thursday in Boufarik, 30 (20 miles) south of Algiers. Twenty more were killed 12 days ago in two car bomb attacks in Algiers and the eastern town of Ain-Fakroun.

The killings of 36 people in Sidi Abdelaziz village in Medea followed a a massacre on November 6 when Moslem rebels cut the throats of 31 villagers in Sidi el Kebir hamlet, near the garrison town of Blida.
Moslem guerrillas slaughtered 14 villagers a week ago in Tabainat village, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.

The flare-up of violence followed the fifth anniversary of the annullment of a general election on January 12. Guerrillas have stepped up attacks during Ramadan as they believe the month is fitting for their "holy war" against the Algerian government.
About 60,000 people have died in Algerian violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election which radical Islamists were about to win.
